`fb_select()` is a
recent addition, and its arguments and output may change.

`fb_select()` starts from a fitted mixed model and a list of candidate
covariates, and asks which candidates improve predictions for new sites. The
fixed effects already in the model are *protected*: they are never shrunk or
dropped. The candidates share a shrinkage prior, and the choice between them
is scored on folds that hold out whole sites. A shrinkage posterior has no
coefficients exactly equal to zero, so "selected" always means chosen by a
stated rule.

# Data

Twenty sites with ten plots each, and eight candidate covariates. Only `x1`
and `x2` affect the response.


``` r
set.seed(20260912)

n_site <- 20L
per_site <- 10L
site <- factor(rep(sprintf("S%02d", seq_len(n_site)), each = per_site))
n <- length(site)

d <- data.frame(site = site)
for (v in paste0("x", 1:8)) {
  d[[v]] <- stats::rnorm(n)
}
u <- stats::setNames(stats::rnorm(n_site, sd = 0.8), levels(site))

d$y <- 2 + 1.2 * d$x1 - 0.9 * d$x2 +
  as.numeric(u[as.character(d$site)]) + stats::rnorm(n, sd = 0.6)
```

# The base model

The base model has a random site effect and no fixed effects other than the
intercept. This is needed for the regularised horseshoe prior used below,
which brms applies to every fixed coefficient except the intercept. A base
with protected fixed effects is shown later.


``` r
base <- flexybayes(
  y ~ 1 + (1 | site),
  data = d,
  backend = "brms",
  chains = 2L,
  n_samples = 2000L,
  warmup = 1000L,
  seed = 20260912L,
  verbose = FALSE,
  mcmc_verbose = FALSE
)
#> Loading required namespace: rstan
```

# The prior

`fb_penalty()` takes one formula per block of candidates. `p0` is the prior
guess at how many candidates matter. The posterior can disagree with it.


``` r
pen <- fb_penalty(term(everything()) ~ regularized_horseshoe(p0 = 2))
pen
#> <fb_penalty> 1 specification(s), resolution = "term", scaling = "train_fold_standardize"
#>   1. term(everything()) ~ regularized_horseshoe(p0 = 2, slab_scale = 2, slab_df = 4, df = 1, df_global = 1, scope = "candidates")
#>      route class_wide, hyperparameters learned
#>   columns resolve against the model matrix at fit time.
```

# Plan first

`plan = TRUE` checks the request and reports what would run, without fitting.


``` r
fb_select(
  base,
  candidates = ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8,
  penalty    = pen,
  resamples  = fb_resamples(unit = ~ site, v = 3L),
  plan       = TRUE,
  seed       = 20260912L
)
#> == flexyBayes selection plan ============================
#>   Projection structure gate:
#>     response family           supported  Gaussian response with an identity link
#>     population-level effects  supported  the fixed part is what the search selects over (probe C2)
#>     (1 | site)                supported  grouped random intercept: get_refmodel() accepted it and a validated grouped k-fold search ran (probes C1-C3)
#>   Workflow:     bayes
#>   Provider:     brms
#>   Prior:        regularized_horseshoe  (route class_wide)
#>   Decision:     projection (resolved from "auto")
#>                 every structural feature of the reference model has an executed projection gate behind it, so the decision is the projection
#>                  the search runs on 20 clustered draws and the predictive evaluation on 100
#>   Candidates:   x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7, x8
#>   Prior blocks:
#>     1. term(everything()) ~ regularized_horseshoe over 8 coefficient(s), learned hyperparameters
#>   stanvars:     no
#>   Structure gate: supported
#>   Folds:        3, prediction new_cluster
#>   Cost estimate: 53.2s over 4 fit(s) at 13.30s each
#>                  the per-fit figure is the base model's own recorded wall time; the reference model carries a wider fixed part and a shrinkage prior, so this is a floor
#>   Approximations this route commits to:
#>     - calibration_n_at_the_resampling_unit: the prior scales are calibrated against 20 units of site rather than against 200 rows, because rows inside a cluster are not independent pieces of evidence about a coefficient
#>     - projection_search_folds_reuse_whole_sample_preprocessing: the projection's k-fold search refits the reference model through brms, which reuses the reference fit's standardised data, compiled prior and calibration, so the constants and prior scales inside the search's folds are the whole sample's and the elpd-by-size curve that chooses the submodel is not strictly out of fold. The benchmark's out-of-fold tables learn every constant on each fold's analysis rows
#>   Nothing was fitted.
```

# Selection

The reference model with all eight candidates is fitted to all the data and
again in each fold. projpred then projects it onto smaller models, and the rule `"one_se"` picks the smallest
model whose predictive score is within one standard error of the best. A
horseshoe prior needs `adapt_delta = 0.99` here to avoid divergent
transitions, which makes the fit slower.

projpred prints convergence warnings from its submodel fits. They are hidden
on this page.


``` r
sel <- fb_select(
  base,
  candidates = ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8,
  penalty    = pen,
  resamples  = fb_resamples(unit = ~ site, v = 3L),
  decision   = fb_decision(method = "projection", rule = "one_se"),
  engine     = list(chains = 4L, n_samples = 1500L,
                    warmup = 1500L, adapt_delta = 0.99),
  seed       = 20260912L
)
#> Warning: 49 of 6000 (1.0%) transitions hit the maximum treedepth limit of 10.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Setting 'K' to the number of folds (3)
#> Fitting model 1 out of 3
#> Warning: 11 of 6000 (0.0%) transitions hit the maximum treedepth limit of 10.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Fitting model 2 out of 3
#> Warning: 1 of 6000 (0.0%) transitions hit the maximum treedepth limit of 10.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Fitting model 3 out of 3
#> Warning: 6 of 6000 (0.0%) transitions hit the maximum treedepth limit of 10.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

sel
#> <fb_select> workflow bayes / provider brms / prior regularized_horseshoe / decision projection, searched on 20 clustered draws and evaluated on 100
#>   Projection structure gate:
#>     response family           supported  Gaussian response with an identity link
#>     population-level effects  supported  the fixed part is what the search selects over (probe C2)
#>     (1 | site)                supported  grouped random intercept: get_refmodel() accepted it and a validated grouped k-fold search ran (probes C1-C3)
#>   base      : gaussian/identity, 200 rows, convergence ok
#>   prior n   : calibrated at 20 site, not at 200 rows
#>   covariance: none: covariance integrated by the engine / integrated (integrated by the engine, not plugged in)
#>   resampling: 3 folds, prediction new_cluster, scored at site
#>   reference : adequacy pass -- 49 transition(s) reached the treedepth ceiling of 10; reported, not decisive
#> 
#>   decision  : projection
#>     size    : 3  ((1 | site), x1, x2)
#> 
#>   approximations:
#>     - calibration_n_at_the_resampling_unit: the prior scales are calibrated against 20 units of site rather than against 200 rows, because rows inside a cluster are not independent pieces of evidence about a coefficient
#>     - projection_search_folds_reuse_whole_sample_preprocessing: the projection's k-fold search refits the reference model through brms, which reuses the reference fit's standardised data, compiled prior and calibration, so the constants and prior scales inside the search's folds are the whole sample's and the elpd-by-size curve that chooses the submodel is not strictly out of fold. The benchmark's out-of-fold tables learn every constant on each fold's analysis rows
```

errors computed over sites:

``` r
rnd(sel$projection$elpd_by_size[, c("size", "elpd", "se", "delta_to_ref")])
```

``` r
plot(sel, type = "elpd_by_size")
```

``` r
sel$selection$chosen_terms
#> [1] "(1 | site)" "x1"         "x2"
```

`tidy()` gives the reference posterior for each candidate. These are not the
estimates of the chosen submodel.


``` r
rnd(tidy(sel)[, c("term", "role", "estimate", "std.error", "retained")])
#>          term      role estimate std.error retained
#> 1 (Intercept) protected       NA        NA     TRUE
#> 2          x1 candidate    1.273     0.042     TRUE
#> 3          x2 candidate   -0.888     0.040     TRUE
#> 4          x3 candidate   -0.006     0.028    FALSE
#> 5          x4 candidate   -0.020     0.032    FALSE
#> 6          x5 candidate   -0.016     0.032    FALSE
#> 7          x6 candidate    0.040     0.040    FALSE
#> 8          x7 candidate   -0.021     0.032    FALSE
#> 9          x8 candidate    0.003     0.028    FALSE
```

# A base with protected fixed effects

Most real models protect some fixed effects, such as a treatment. The
horseshoe on its own covers every fixed effect, so use `laplace()`,
`ridge()` or `elastic_net()`, which put a prior on each candidate separately,
or `regularized_horseshoe(scope = "block")`, which fits the candidates as
their own part of the model and leaves the protected effects outside it.


``` r
d$p1 <- stats::rnorm(nrow(d))
d$y_p <- d$y + 0.7 * d$p1

protected_base <- flexybayes(
  y_p ~ p1 + (1 | site),
  data = d,
  backend = "brms",
  chains = 2L,
  n_samples = 2000L,
  warmup = 1000L,
  seed = 20260912L,
  verbose = FALSE,
  mcmc_verbose = FALSE
)

protected_sel <- fb_select(
  protected_base,
  candidates = ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8,
  penalty    = fb_penalty(term(everything()) ~ laplace(scale = 0.3)),
  resamples  = fb_resamples(unit = ~ site, v = 3L),
  decision   = fb_decision(method = "full"),
  engine     = list(chains = 4L, n_samples = 1500L, warmup = 1500L),
  seed       = 20260912L
)

rnd(tidy(protected_sel)[, c("term", "role", "family", "estimate")])
#>           term      role  family estimate
#> 1  (Intercept) protected    none       NA
#> 2           p1 protected    none    0.754
#> 3           x1 candidate laplace    1.266
#> 4           x2 candidate laplace   -0.889
#> 5           x3 candidate laplace   -0.005
#> 6           x4 candidate laplace   -0.041
#> 7           x5 candidate laplace   -0.038
#> 8           x6 candidate laplace    0.067
#> 9           x7 candidate laplace   -0.044
#> 10          x8 candidate laplace    0.005
```

`p1` has no shrinkage prior. The same request with the horseshoe stops:


``` r
fb_select(
  protected_base,
  candidates = ~ x1 + x2,
  penalty    = fb_penalty(term(everything()) ~ regularized_horseshoe(p0 = 1)),
  resamples  = fb_resamples(unit = ~ site, v = 3L),
  plan       = TRUE,
  seed       = 20260912L
)
#> Error:
#> ! fb_penalty(): regularized_horseshoe() is a class-wide prior -- brms applies it to every population-level coefficient except the intercept -- and these coefficients are outside the block: p1. Three ways forward: use ridge(), laplace() or elastic_net(), which target blocks exactly; write regularized_horseshoe(scope = "block"), which fits the candidates as their own non-linear part and leaves those coefficients under their own priors, with the full or posterior-threshold decision; or write regularized_horseshoe(scope = "all_fixed"), an explicit opt-in under which those coefficients also sit under the global-local prior, the projection search forces them into every submodel, and the certificate records approximations = "protected_under_global_shrinkage".
```

# Without a shrinkage prior

`penalty = NULL` fits the base model with and without the candidates in each
fold, and compares their predictions for the held-out sites. Here the
base is fitted with INLA.


``` r
d$y2 <- d$y + 0.4 * d$p1

inla_base <- flexybayes(
  y2 ~ p1,
  random  = ~ site,
  data    = d,
  backend = "inla",
  verbose = FALSE
)

increment <- fb_select(
  inla_base,
  candidates = ~ x1 + x2,
  resamples  = fb_resamples(unit = ~ site, v = 3L),
  seed       = 20260912L
)

rnd(glance(increment)[, c(
  "loss", "loss_protected_only", "loss_full", "loss_reduction", "n_units"
)])
#>       loss loss_protected_only loss_full loss_reduction n_units
#> 1 neg_elpd              20.088    13.956          6.132      20
```

The scores are held-out losses, so lower is better. `neg_elpd` is minus the
log predictive density of a held-out site, and `loss_reduction` is the loss
without the candidates minus the loss with them.

A shrinkage prior on an INLA base is fitted with brms, since INLA does not
fit these priors.

# Other options

- `benchmark = TRUE` adds two non-Bayesian comparisons on the same folds:
  generalised least squares and `glmnet`.
- `workflow = "penalized_optimizer"` computes a penalised path directly,
  which is much faster than sampling. `vignette("flexyBayes-06-two-stage")`
  uses it.
- `sel$certificate` records what was fitted, by which engine, under which
  prior and rule.

# Which prior on which base

| Prior | Base with protected fixed effects | Projection |
|---|---|---|
| `ridge()`, `laplace()`, `elastic_net()` | yes | yes |
| `regularized_horseshoe()`, `r2d2()` | only with `scope = "all_fixed"`, which shrinks the protected effects too | yes |
| any prior, on a base with `vm()` or `ped()` | yes | no (the default `decision = "auto"` uses `"full"`) |
